title: Stanford Alpaca
authors: R. Taori, I. Gulrajani, T. Zhang, et al.
before: Instruction tuning was assumed to need industrial resources and proprietary data.
problem: Could a university group turn a base model into an assistant for pocket change?
breakthrough: 52,000 self-instruct examples generated from text-davinci-003, used to fine-tune LLaMA 7B for a few hundred dollars.
why: It showed capability could be distilled cheaply from a stronger model, which set off the open fine-tune explosion and the licensing fights.
next: Vicuna and dozens of derivatives; distillation became standard practice and a terms-of-service problem.
inherits: Cheap instruction tuning by distilling from a stronger model.
